title: Rosetta entry (T3)
description: One source system read once, under stated forcing. Mirrors the stdlib validator in src/rosetta_shape_core/entry.py — that module is the runtime check; this file is the contract for anything outside Python. Entries are markers to explore, not positions defended.

id.description: Stable handle. Derived from source_system when absent. Never renamed — see the gate log rule in gate_log.py.

source_system.description: crystal, grass, mycelium, ... The system that solved a structurally similar problem under different constraints.

configuration.description: What it reaches under constraint. A behaviour readout — no intent attribution, no moral label.

forcing_terms.description: Family ids or aliases (see families.py). This field is what licenses transfer: shared forcing means the shape is caused, not resembled.

forcing_dominant.description: The subset of forcing_terms that SETS the configuration. Presence of a shared term is too cheap a test to license transfer on its own — strain acts on nearly everything. Every member must also appear in forcing_terms.

move_ported.description: The transferable operation. The move, not the ontology.

stops.description: Where it stops. An entry that produces everywhere and never stops is the audit flag, not a strong entry. A stop may be a plain string or an object with an id, and it needs an explicit id before a transfer or observation can reference it.

provenance.description: Where this record came from. concept = where the thing being recorded came from; record = who wrote the record text as it stands. A repo that demands operand provenance of what it reads does not ship unmarked records of its own. See src/rosetta_shape_core/provenance.py.

shape_token.description: The name used. Carries no literal/stand-in flag by design: reason from the shape's formal properties and the failure grades the token (see scope.py).

gate_history.description: Dated record of which register a name had to unlock. Data on the models.
